transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-01-30 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Linnea (Redwood SE), Maya (TorrentTech CTO), Ethan (Head of ML), Priya (Infra)

Summary:
- Kickoff to scope a 4-6 week pilot to validate latency & unit economics for TorrentTech's search-assist product. Focus: per-token cost estimates, batching/caching knobs, bench plan and timelines.

Topics:
- Success criteria: p95 latency, throughput, quality regression thresholds, and cost per 1M tokens.
- Workload sizing: QPS, avg prompt length, peak windows.
- Benchmark plan: models to test, metrics, tooling, test dataset.
- Cost model: tokenization, batching, KV caching, quantization options, fallbacks.
- Timeline & next steps.

[00:00] Samir (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining. want to kick off — we scoped this as a pilot to validate both perf and unit economics for your search-assist feature. quick round-robin intros?
[00:20] Maya (TorrentTech): hi, maya here, cto. we run a product that augments developer search results with generated hints — average request is a short query + 120 token context.
[00:35] Ethan (TorrentTech): ethan — ml lead, i'll own the prompt set and evaluation. expect 0.8-1.2 RPS steady-state, spikes to 6-8 RPS with peak traffic during deploys.
[00:50] Priya (TorrentTech): priya, infra. main constraints: we have a 25k/month cloud budget for inference initially and strict data residency for EU.
[01:05] Samir: great. linnea and i will map that to throughput targets and a cost runway. linnea, quick on workload sizing?
[01:15] Linnea (Redwood): sure — from what they said: avg prompt length ~120 tokens, we should capture average generation length (say 80 tokens) so overall token per call ~200 tokens. at 1 RPS sustained that's about 17.3M tokens/mo (1*60*60*24*30 * 200 ~= 518M? wait hangon math).
[01:45] Ethan: (laughs) the math there — maybe re-run.
[01:50] Linnea: sorry scrub — my mental math off. correct calc: 1 RPS * 86400 s/day * 30 days = 2.592M requests/mo * 200 tokens = ~518M tokens/mo. ok, so at steady 1 RPS it's half a billion tokens. with your 25k$/mo budget that matters.
[02:15] Maya: exact traffic will vary but spike-aware autoscaling + batching is key. we don't want to overprovision.
[02:30] Samir: high-level cost levers we'll use: model family (base vs. instruction-tuned), batching window & max batch size, KV/prefix caching for repeated contexts, and quantized model variants on Dedicated or Private. also routing (hosted low-latency vs dedicated cheaper per-token).
[03:00] Linnea: for the bench plan: we propose testing 3 model variants — mid-size open model (compatibility baseline), quantized 8-bit on dedicated, and a hosted optimized variant. metrics: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens, and quality (ROUGE/BLEU-ish + human eval sample).
[03:30] Ethan: can we get example per-token numbers? even rough ballpark so we can sanity check budget.
[03:38] Samir: yes — rough illustrative: hosted optimized model ~ $0.90 per 1M input tokens + $1.20 per 1M output tokens — so roughly $2.10 per 1M tokens if you count both sides. dedicated quantized path can be ~ $0.6–1.0 per 1M tokens depending on utilization and batching. these are illustrative; we'll send precise sheet.
[04:05] Priya: what's driving the delta? is it GPU amortization or infra?
[04:12] Linnea: mainly amortization and kernel-level optimizations; also batching efficiency — larger batches reduce cost per token but increase p95. KV cache reduces repeat generation costs by avoiding re-computation of shared contexts.
[04:30] Maya: explain KV cash? i heard kv cash from a webinar — how reliable is it for our use case?
[04:37] Linnea: (laughs) kv cash = kv cache — sorry. it's good when a lot of requests share prefixes/context, e.g., same doc snippets. it stores computed key-value pairs from attention so repeated prefixes skip those tokens. effective when the same 50-200 token prefix repeats.
[05:05] Ethan: our prompts vary but we have a lot of overlap — 30-40% of tokens could be cached. that's compelling.
[05:20] Samir: ok, benchmark plan details: 1) you give canonical prompt set (Ethan) — 1k examples, 2) Redwood will run harness against 3 model configs for two load shapes (steady 1 RPS, spike 8 RPS) for 48 hours each. we'll capture per-token cost estimates, p50/p95 latency, and failure rates.
[05:45] Linnea: we'll also include a run with prefix caching enabled to quantify delta. and a run for aggressive batching (batch size cap 128) vs conservative batching (cap 8) to show latency/cost trade.
[06:05] Priya: what's the expected added latency from batching? p95 ballpark?
[06:10] Linnea: conservative: p95 ~200-300ms; aggressive batching p95 could go to 600-800ms depending on batch window and queueing. those are rough. we can aim for p95 < 350ms for user-facing interactions.
[06:30] Samir: success criteria (proposed): 1) p95 generation latency < 350ms on steady load for chosen config, 2) throughput meets 1 RPS steady and handles 8 RPS spikes with graceful degradation, 3) cost per 1M tokens under $X (we agreed to set $X = $1,200? No that's not right) — let's define a percent of their 25k budget.
[06:55] Maya: our constraint: we want to keep inference < $12k/mo initially for 25k total cloud spend — so let's target inference budget of 12k. if we hit 518M tokens/mo we need per-token to be roughly <= $0.023 /1000? this is messy, can you translate?
[07:20] Linnea: quick calc: 518M tokens / 1M = 518 units. To spend $12k, cost per 1M tokens must be <= $23.17. so $23 per 1M tokens. that is much higher than the earlier examples because those were $0.6–2 per 1M? hmm, we're mixing units — i think earlier numbers were dollars per million tokens of model compute only; we need to be careful with input vs output tokens and units. we'll send a clear spreadsheet.
[07:55] Ethan: yes please send the worked examples.
[08:00] Samir: action: we'll produce three scenarios in the sheet: 'hosted low-latency', 'dedicated quantized', and 'hosted + caching' showing cost per 1M and monthly projection at your traffic shape.
[08:15] Linnea: about timelines: propose 1 week to align on prompts & infra requirements, 2 weeks to run bench & iterate, 1 week for analysis and follow-up workshop = ~4 weeks. if security review is fast, we can shorten.
[08:35] Priya: security: we need SOC 2 evidence, residency for EU, and KMS integration. can Redwood run on a VPC or provide Private?
[08:45] Samir: yes — Redwood Private can run in your VPC or as on-prem package. for pilot, we can run the benchmark on Redwood Hosted with encryption + EU region tenancy; if you want guaranteed residency and no shared infra, Dedicated/Private is available but adds setup time.
[09:05] Maya: what's the extra setup time for Private?
[09:10] Linnea: typically 3-6 weeks depending on networking and KMS exchange. Dedicated (reserved pools) could be faster if you accept our managed infra in EU region — maybe 2-4 weeks.
[09:25] Ethan: for benchmark we prefer hosted in EU region to move fast. then if results look good we'll plan Private later.
[09:30] Samir: perfect. we'll limit sensitive data during bench, use synthetic or redacted contexts.
[09:40] Linnea: benchmarks we run will include: cold-start latency, steady-state p95, token throughput, GPU utilization, and cost breakdown (kernel time, batching efficiency, network).
[09:55] Maya: any risk of model quality regression when moving to quantized?
[10:00] Linnea: small regressions can occur; Redwood Optimize recommends quantization profiles per model and we'll run our evals to measure quality delta. if quality drops beyond your threshold (we should set a threshold like <5% drop on human-rated accuracy), we won't push that config to production.
[10:25] Ethan: set quality threshold to max 3% drop on our core QA tasks.
[10:30] Samir: noted. we'll add that to success criteria.
[10:40] Maya: how do retries and fallbacks affect cost? if we route to a cheaper fallback model on load, is there extra cost?
[10:50] Linnea: fallback adds some orchestration cost but can reduce spend if the fallback is cheaper. we model fallback hits in the spreadsheet. also automatic routing by policy (latency vs cost) will be part of the pilot configuration.
[11:05] Samir: quick note on observability — Redwood Console provides token-level cost breakdown and request traces; we'll share demo access for the pilot.
[11:20] Priya: we need audit logs for compliance.
[11:23] Samir: yes we can provide audit logs and integration with your SIEM via webhook/HTTP delivery.
[11:35] Ethan: sample prompts — we'll include 1k canonical prompts and mark which ones are short vs long so you can run stratified bench.
[11:45] Linnea: perfect. we'll also include a script to replay traffic shapes (Poisson + peak spike) so we can simulate realistic queueing.
[11:55] Maya: what's the expected pilot cost to run the bench? small fixed fee?
[12:00] Samir: for a 48-hour, 3-config benchmark we typically bill a modest bench fee to cover compute — approx $2k-$3k depending on EU region GPU hours. we can offset against pilot if you convert. we'll put that in the sheet.
[12:20] Priya: ok — operationally we need a statement of work and an IP/data handling addendum.
[12:28] Samir: we'll attach a short SOW + security addendum to the follow-up email.
[12:35] Linnea: one more technical: we should capture the distribution of sequence lengths because kernel selection depends a lot on max seq and kv cache hit rate. please include percentiles (p50, p90, p99) of prompt+response lengths.
[12:55] Ethan: will do.
[13:05] Maya: recap and next steps?
[13:10] Samir: recap: 1) TorrentTech to share 1k prompt set + traffic profile (Ethan) by 2026-02-03, 2) Redwood to send cost spreadsheet + bench plan by 2026-02-02 (Samir & Linnea), 3) schedule pilot planning meeting week of 2026-02-08. bench to run in EU hosted region, 3 model configs, include kv cache run and batching variants.
[13:40] Maya: sounds good. also add security SOW and KMS checklist.
[13:50] Samir: will do. we'll include link to shared artifacts: pricing spreadsheet + bench harness: https://redwood.app/sheets/torrent-pilot and harness repo: https://git.redwood/repo/torrent-bench (access by invite).
[14:05] Ethan: thanks all, that was productive.

Questions captured:
- How much can KV cache realistically reduce cost for our workload? (Ethan)
- What is the bench fee and how is it credited? (Priya)
- Timeline for Private deployment if pilot succeeds? (Maya)

Recap / Next steps (same as action items):
- Samir to send cost spreadsheet + SOW + security addendum (due 2026-02-02).
- Linnea to share benchmark harness and runbook (due 2026-02-04).
- Ethan to provide prompt set & traffic profile (due 2026-02-03).

End of transcript.
